 Q3 revenue rose 19.1% year over year to CNY 24.28 billion , with deliveries up 15% sequentially and vehicle margin improving to 13.1%. XPENG's net loss narrowed from the prior quarter to CNY 0.87 billion, while overall gross margin slipped to 18.9%. 
 XPENG forecast record Q4 deliveries of 169,000–174,000 vehicles and revenue of CNY 30.4–31.8 billion. It is targeting more than 100,000 overseas sales in 2026 and expects those sales to more than double in 2027, despite export-tax changes and other cost pressures. 
 The company plans to begin commercial deliveries of its IRON humanoid robot in Q2 2027 and is developing robotaxi services, with operations expected to scale from 2028. Management also cited AI memory-chip costs, export tax changes, and a battery consumption tax as potential challenges.

 XPENG (NYSE:XPEV) reported higher third-quarter revenue and a narrower sequential loss as vehicle deliveries and average selling prices rose, while management projected record deliveries and revenue for the final quarter of 2026. 
 The electric vehicle maker also outlined plans to more than double overseas sales in 2027 and begin commercial deliveries of its IRON humanoid robot. Executives said international growth could improve profitability, although they identified costs and changes to export tax rebates as challenges. 
 Revenue rises as vehicle margins improve 
 → MarketBeat Week in Review – 11/9 - 11/13 
 XPeng's Top Secret AI Robotics Program Outshines EV Woes 
 Third-quarter revenue increased 19.1% from a year earlier to CNY 24.28 billion and rose 23% from the second quarter. Vehicle sales revenue climbed 19.8% year over year to CNY 21.63 billion, helped by higher deliveries and an improved model mix, Vice President of Finance and Accounting James Wu said. 
 XPENG delivered 118,390 vehicles in the quarter, up 15% from the preceding three months. Vehicle margin rose to 13.1% from 12.1% in the second quarter and was unchanged from a year earlier. Overall gross margin fell to 18.9%, compared with 20.7% in the second quarter and 20.1% a year earlier.

 Smart Money Is Buying Auto Suppliers, Not Car Brands 
 Wu said the sequential decline in overall gross margin partly reflected the absence of a major technical research and development services milestone from XPENG's Volkswagen collaboration that had contributed revenue in the second quarter. Higher carbon credit sales partly offset that effect, he said. 
 Story Continues The company posted a net loss of CNY 0.87 billion, compared with a CNY 0.38 billion loss a year earlier and a CNY 1.34 billion loss in the second quarter. Its operating loss was CNY 0.75 billion, unchanged from a year earlier and narrower than the CNY 1.14 billion loss in the preceding quarter. Cash stood at CNY 45.41 billion as of September 30. 
 Fourth-quarter outlook and overseas expansion

 XPENG expects fourth-quarter deliveries of approximately 169,000 to 174,000 vehicles, an increase of 45.4% to 49.7% from a year earlier. It forecast revenue of CNY 30.4 billion to CNY 31.8 billion, up 36.6% to 42.9%. 
 Co-founder, Chairman and CEO He Xiaopeng said monthly deliveries surpassed 50,000 for the first time in October and that the company expects monthly sales to exceed 60,000 in November. He said deliveries of the MONA L03 exceeded 20,000 in October, while the MONA L05, launched in late October, was expected to exceed 10,000 deliveries in its first month. 
 Overseas sales reached 13,000 vehicles in October, up 166% year over year, He said. XPENG is targeting more than 40,000 overseas sales in the fourth quarter and more than 100,000 for all of 2026. For 2027, it expects overseas sales to more than double and its international sales network to exceed 1,000 stores. 
 Vice Chairman and President Brian Gu estimated that Europe would account for around half or more of overseas volume next year, followed by Southeast Asia and Asia Pacific at approximately 30%, and the Middle East and Latin America at about 20%. 
 Wu said export vehicle gross margin was more than double that of the domestic business in the third quarter. To address changes to export tax rebates, the company is considering measures including faster overseas localization, pricing adjustments and changes to its product cadence. Gu said XPENG already has manufacturing partnerships in Austria, Malaysia and Indonesia and is looking to expand its overseas production footprint. 
 Robot and autonomous driving plans 
 He said XPENG's first automated production line for general-purpose humanoid robots began operating in September. The company plans trial deployment of its first mass-produced IRON robots in some XPENG stores in the first quarter of 2027, followed by an external commercial launch in the second quarter. 
 During the question-and-answer session, He said XPENG intends to develop a standardized robot for small and medium-sized business customers and eventually households, rather than rely on customized products. He emphasized hardware, mass production, data and computing capabilities as areas of focus. 
 XPENG also received approval for Level 4 robotaxi demonstrations across Guangzhou and has launched XPENG YOYO as its robotaxi service brand, He said. The company plans to offer end-to-end solutions to global partners next year and expects YOYO operations to begin scaling in 2028, starting overseas. 
 Wu declined to provide 2027 earnings guidance, saying it was too early. He said the company expects its full-year 2026 gross margin to be in the high teens, while citing AI-related memory chip costs, export tax changes and a battery consumption tax among potential challenges. 
 About XPENG (NYSE:XPEV) 
 XPENG Inc. is a Chinese electric vehicle company that designs, develops, manufactures and sells smart electric vehicles. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Guangzhou, the company focuses on combining vehicle engineering with software and technology features. Its product lineup includes electric sedans, SUVs and multipurpose vehicles. XPENG also develops driver-assistance technologies, in-car software and related services, and operates charging infrastructure to support its vehicles. The company primarily serves customers in China and has expanded into international markets.
